Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1227 PM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM SOUTHERN
GEORGIA INTO MUCH OF NORTHERN FLORIDA INCLUDING THE PANHANDLE...AND
FROM FAR EASTERN MONTANA INTO PARTS OF THE WESTERN DAKOTAS...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered severe storms capable of mainly damaging winds are
possible Wednesday afternoon and early evening over southern
Georgia, northern Florida and the Florida Panhandle. Isolated severe
storms capable of damaging gusts and large hail may occur over the
northern High Plains Wednesday afternoon and evening.

...Southern GA and AL...Northern FL and the FL Panhandle...
A slow moving upper trough will begin to weaken/fill on Wednesday
over the eastern states, with upper low centered over NY. A cold
front will primarily be offshore, but the tail end will extend
westward across GA/FL. Ahead of the front, 70s F dewpoints and
strong heating will lead to strong instability, with MLCAPE possibly
reaching 4000 J/kg. This high PWAT environment along with favorable
time of day near peak heating will yield severe wind potential as
storms develop near the cold front during the afternoon.

While shear will be weak, modest westerly mean winds aloft should
support a general southeastward storm motion with multicells and
merging outflows expected. The primary concentration of storms
should be from far southern GA into the FL Panhandle and northern
FL, and perhaps into far southeast AL. Additional daytime activity
is likely farther northwest across MA and AR as well, though
large-scale support will be less. Still, areas of strong instability
could yield scattered strong gusts there.

...Northern High Plains...
A surface trough will deepen from eastern MT into WY during the
afternoon with strong heating and steep low-level lapse rates
developing. This area will also be affected by a disturbance aloft
rounding the upper ridge and enhancing mid/upper winds and
deep-layer shear. Southeasterly low-level winds will maintain
sufficient moisture into the region to support 1000-1500 J/kg MLCAPE
even as the boundary layer mixes with heating. Storms will form over
eastern MT and WY after 21Z and move into the western Dakotas
through early evening, with damaging wind potential. Isolated hail
may occur as well as mid/upper lapse rates remain steep, and high
level winds increase, elongating hodographs.

..Jewell.. 07/28/2026

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE NORTHERN TO CENTRAL PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Sporadic occurrences of mainly damaging wind appear possible
Thursday afternoon and night across parts of the northern and
central Plains.

...Discussion...
On Thursday, the pattern will feature an upper trough over the East
with filling low over the Northeast, and an upper high from the
Southwest into the Four Corners states. In between, a modest
northwest flow regime will exist over much of the Plains, with
embedded disturbances forecast over the northern and central Plains.

During the afternoon, a surface trough will develop from eastern MT
into the OK/TX Panhandles, where strong heating will occur. A
pre-frontal trough will also develop from SD into MN ahead of a cold
front trailing southwestward out of Ontario. This area may be
favorable timed with a weak wave moving around the upper ridge, and
storms that form within the surface trough will be capable of
sporadic severe hail or wind given 2000+ MUCAPE and deep-layer shear
around 30 kt. Possible early day thunderstorms complicate the
forecast setup, but a Slight Risk may eventually be added over the
northern Plains as predictability increases.

..Jewell.. 07/28/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0314 AM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Valid 311200Z - 051200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Friday...

The 00Z models have trended toward a more intense short-wave trough
over the Midwest, which in turn leads to a deeper surface low
tracking toward the mid MS Valley. However, the progression of those
features will be toward an area of more persistent surface ridging
with only an axis of modest instability forecast ahead of the
surface low. Stronger instability is expected to reside farther
southwest from the lower MO Valley into the Ozark Plateau, ahead of
a southeastward-moving cold front. A few severe storms appear
possible from the vicinity of the surface low southwest along the
cold front. But, given the northward displacement of the stronger
forcing for ascent and vertical shear from the stronger instability,
the degree of organized severe weather potential remains uncertain. 


Elsewhere, an isolated severe weather threat could materialize over
the northern and central High Plains within a moist, low-level
upslope regime.


...Day 5/Saturday...

The Day 4 short-wave trough is forecast to develop through the mid
MS into lower OH Valley along with the surface low. Meanwhile, the
trailing cold front will advance southeast into the lower MS Valley,
where moderate to strong instability is forecast by afternoon. A few
severe storms appear possible along and ahead of the front; however,
generally weak vertical shear is expected to limit the potential for
a more organized event. 

...Day 6-8/Sunday through Tuesday...

Both the ensemble means and deterministic models remain in
relatively good agreement in depicting a stronger short-wave trough
and attending belt of mid-level flow progressing along the
international border from the northern Rockies to the northern
Plains in the Sunday-Monday time frame. Some severe weather threat
could materialize along an associated cold front over ND on Sunday
and the northern Plains into the upper MS Valley on Monday as
strengthening vertical shear overspreads an unstable warm sector. By
Tuesday, the front is expected to stall over the central High Plains
with some severe weather threat possible within the post-frontal
upslope regime.

..Mead.. 07/28/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1119 AM CDT Tue Jul 28 2026

Valid 281630Z - 291200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM EAST
TENNESSEE INTO THE MID ATLANTIC REGION AND CAROLINAS...AND OVER
EASTERN COLORADO...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms capable of severe wind gusts and a tornado threat are
expected today from parts of the Mid-Atlantic southward into the
Carolinas. A few severe wind gusts and hail may also occur this
afternoon and evening across parts of the central High Plains.

...East TN into central VA/NC...
Late morning thunderstorms persist over parts of this region, with
pockets of precip and clouds.  This will somewhat limit afternoon
heating across NC, but upstream heating and ample moisture should
spread eastward.  This will aid in the re-development of intense
thunderstorms later today across the mountains of east TN/KY into
southwest VA and western NC.  Forecast soundings show considerable
low and deep layer shear, favorable for supercell and bowing
structures.  Damaging winds are the main concern, but hail and a few
tornadoes are also possible if supercells are maintained.  These
storms will spread southeastward into central NC during the evening
with a continued damaging wind risk.

...Central VA into parts of PA/DE/NJ...
Persistent cloud cover is limiting daytime heating so far from
eastern PA eastward to the coast.  However, visible satellite
imagery shows some clearing developing from central PA into central
VA, where temperatures are climbing rapidly into the 80s.  This
trend will likely spread eastward and aid in the development of
scattered afternoon storms.  Relatively steep mid-level lapse rates
and sufficient winds aloft will promote damaging winds in the
strongest cores.  Occasional supercell structures could also result
in a tornado or two and/or hail.

...Eastern CO...
An upper ridge is centered over northern NM, with 20-30 knot
westerly flow over northern CO/southern WY.  Scattered thunderstorms
are expected to form over the mountains and foothills today,
spreading eastward into the plains by late afternoon.  Ample
moisture and moderate CAPE over the mountains, along with sufficient
vertical shear, may support hail in the strongest cells.  As the
activity moves eastward into a hot air mass, locally damaging winds
will become a risk.  This activity may spread into western NE/KS
this evening before weakening.

..Hart/Moore.. 07/28/2026
